== Biography ==
=== Irish-family context, 24 October 2026 ===

The selected father [[Glasgow-1024|James Glasgow]] remains '''35% (possible)''' for [[Glasgow-649|Arthur]]. The separate Irish family is now assessed as probable: [[Glasgow-1024|James]] → [[Glasgow-1025|James]], 78%; [[Glasgow-1492|Samuel]] → [[Glasgow-1025|James]], 76%; [[Glasgow-2426|William]] → [[Glasgow-1025|James]], 84%; and [[Glasgow-2425|Robert]] → [[Glasgow-1025|James]], 77%. Faris’s printed pp.8–12 and the full-letter genealogy identify four sons of James and Margaret Rutherford. These Irish relationships are separate from the unresolved identification of the American emigrants’ father. Faris’s dotted connection to the emigrants and his statement that their parentage had not been established remain material limits.<ref name="IrishFamilyContext20261024">David Faris, ''The Glasgow Family of Adams County, Ohio'' (1990), printed pp.8–12, FamilySearch film 2055438, Item 5, DGS 007834162; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CS3J-H9FN-6 pp.10–11], [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CS3J-H9VW-9 pp.12–13]. [https://www.genealogy.com/forum/surnames/topics/rutherford/5445/ Published full-letter transcription of PRONI T1959/3], read 20 October 2026; original letter uninspected. Samuel’s 1824 will is known here through Faris’s excerpt, not the manuscript.</ref>

The Irish Robert is not thereby the emigrant Robert born in 1749. American sibling grades and all maternal identities retain their existing assessments. The older James-1025 → [[Glasgow-1026|Scottish William]] hypothesis remains 32%. Earlier statements that the Irish James and Samuel links remained 18% and 23% describe the superseded review; they do not represent the current Irish-family assessment. No stronger American father connection follows from the Irish review.

=== Current family assessment, 23 October 2026 ===

The actual Faris book has now been inspected, rather than only its catalogue abstract. Printed p.11 uses a dotted possible connection from James of Moneymore to the American brothers; p.12 explicitly reports that evidence for Robert and his brothers’ parentage had not been found. James was the author’s identifiable County Londonderry candidate, not an evidenced father. The retrospective Irish pedigree on pp.8–9 and Samuel’s 1824 Pennsylvania will discussed on p.12 identify an Irish sibling group, including William, James and Robert remaining in Ireland, without joining it to the emigrant brothers. County setting, a compatible generation and the existing family tradition keep James a plausible candidate, but cannot sustain the earlier probable father assessment. Existing father-profile propositions only: [[Glasgow-12|Robert]] 85% → 35%; [[Glasgow-649|Arthur]] and [[Glasgow-1543|Joseph]] each 82% → 35%; [[Glasgow-4027|John]] 76% → 30%; [[Glasgow-4030|Mary]] 64% → 22%. All five were probable; the first four are now possible and Mary uncertain. [[Glasgow-1024|James]] remains the selected named candidate; no attachment is removed. [[Glasgow-1024|James]]’s own older father stays 18%, and [[Glasgow-1492|Samuel]]’s father stays 23%. '''Historical Irish-only scope:''' the preceding 18%/23% values describe the earlier assessment and are superseded by the 24 October 2026 Irish-family review above. The American father and sibling assessments are unchanged. Mary’s case additionally depends on identifying the 1779 will witness Mary Arter as the emigrant sister. Faris p.13 transmits an unnamed sister styled Mrs Arthur; p.15 identifies Mary Arter with that sister through the tax/probate cluster, rather than an explicit sibling or birth statement. The association remains positive but does not establish her father. Robert, Arthur and Joseph’s established brotherhood remains separately supported by the maintained 1806 letter transcription and Joseph’s 1831 will. John of Peters Township remains a probable brother at 83%; Faris p.15 also reconstructs the four brothers from the 1779–1780 tax/probate cluster. These sibling arguments do not identify their father. The 1824 Samuel will has been read only through Faris’s excerpt, not its manuscript. The Irish Robert in that will/pedigree is not identified as the emigrant Robert born in 1749. All mothers, upstream ancestry, life dates and current attachments are preserved; no live WikiTree save or identity merge follows. Exact percentages are subjective pair-specific judgments, not measured frequencies or multiplied probabilities.<ref>David Faris, The Glasgow Family of Adams County, Ohio (1990), printed pp.8–15; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CS3J-H9VW-9 pp.12–13], [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CS3J-H9FN-6 pp.10–11], [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CS3J-H9FV-S pp.14–15]; FamilySearch film 2055438 Item 5, DGS 007834162, images 1564–1567, visually inspected 23 October 2026. {{1776 Sticker |image=|unit=Rockbridge County Militia, Virginia Militia, American Revolution}}
{{Society Ancestor|Society=DAR|Ancestor=A045298 }}

Arthur was born about 1750. He served as a soldier in Virginia during the Revolution. <ref>{{DAR-grs| A045298 | Arthur Glasgow | 05 Apr 2024}}
</ref>

"Arthur Glasgow died in May 1822, aged 72 years, so he was born in about 1750. He married widow Rebeckah Anderson McNutt McCorkle, on 7 Jan 1782 in Rockbridge County, Virginia.<ref>Arthur Glasgow in the Virginia, U.S., Compiled Marriages, 1660-1800</ref>She was the widow of John McCorkle (died Jan 1781) and the daughter of John McNutt and Katherine Anderson.

According to the source below, "Arthur Glasgow was a descendant of Earl Glasgow, of Scotland," where Arthur emigrated from to our colonies. Oren Frederic Morton's, A History of Rockbridge County, Virginia, Supplement, Staunton, VA, 1920, page 304-306 has some data on Arthur and his family through Alexander McNutt Glasgow. Page 253-254, says the 3 Glasgow brothers, Arthur, Robert and Joseph came to our colonies in the late 1700's. Glasgow Township was named for the family.

Children with Rebeckah:
Joseph Glasgow, 14 Oct 1783
John Glasow, 17 Dec 1785
Ann Nancy Glasgow, 1788,  (Thos McCleland, 1804)
Robert Arthur Glasgow, 1792
Margaret Glasgow, 1793, (Mrs. Edmondson),
Rebecca (John Carr, 1804)

In 1820 he was living in Rockbridge County, Virginia and had 9 slaves.<ref>1820 United States Federal Census for Arthur Glasgow</ref>

He died in May, 1822 and is buried in Falling spring Presbyterian Church Cemetery in Glasgow, Rockbridge County, Virginia.  The date is visible on his headstone.<ref>Arthur Glasgow in the U.S., Find a Grave Index, 1600s-Current</ref>

== Research Notes ==
=== Peters Township family review,20 October 2026 ===

John of Peters Township is assessed as a probable brother at83%. The established Robert–Arthur–Joseph brotherhood and their James-of-Moneymore father ratings are unchanged.

Fendrick’s checked 1944 abstract of the 1779 Peters Township will identifies John Glasgow’s wife Ann, daughters Lates and Agnes, and son Joseph. [[Glasgow-4028|Lates Glasgow]] and [[Glasgow-4029|Joseph Glasgow]] are the existing record-defined daughter and son accounts, not speculative later adult identifications. Assess John as their father at 98% each, strongly supported by the explicit abstracted relationship and matching will context. The manuscript has not been inspected, so this does not certify the spelling or completeness of the abstract. Joseph the son is distinct from the adult Joseph who witnessed the will.

'''Earlier research argument, superseded for fatherhood on 23 October 2026:'''
Assess James of Moneymore, [[Glasgow-1024|James Glasgow II]], as John of Peters Township’s probable father at 76%. The 2024 Adams County family account specifically identifies the John who died in 1779 as brother of Robert, Arthur and Joseph. Fendrick’s abstract independently supplies a contemporary Joseph Glasgow witness in John’s Peters Township will; James Neely’s presence also fits the later Neely-associated emigrant family. Faris’s catalogue description identifies Robert’s father as James of Moneymore and reports four emigrant brothers. Together these identify a specific compatible family, rather than only another local James. Extend that probable father across the preferred fourth-brother identification, while rating John lower than the three established brothers because his place in that group depends partly on the later account and witness identification. Assess the John-to-each-established-brother relationship as probable at 83%.

The original will and probate packet remain uninspected. The checked abstract gives 1779, not the execution/probate days; existing 14 March and 3 September date limits are preserved from the earlier cited profile account, not newly verified. The will index verifies John’s locator, Cumberland Will Book C, p.161, but supplies no relatives. Ann is named as wife, not expressly mother of the children; her existing maternal attachments remain unassessed. Nancy (Glascoe) Wright is only a possible identification of Agnes: an approximately 1778 birth fits a child alive in 1779 and Agnes/Nancy can be compatible name forms, but the later Maryland/Indiana household has no inspected parent, guardianship or estate bridge to Peters Township. Her existing John father is therefore possible at 37%, not confident. The witness Joseph is not proved to be Joseph of Wythe County. The family-history article may depend on Faris and is not independent corroboration of his genealogy. The older James-1025 father of James-1024 remains 18%; no Scottish migration, Mary Harkness maternity, new mother, identity merge or live edit follows. '''Historical Irish-only scope:''' the preceding 18%/23% values describe the earlier assessment and are superseded by the 24 October 2026 Irish-family review above. The American father and sibling assessments are unchanged. === Irish origin and possible collateral family ===

Arthur's approximate 1750 birth is inferred from his age at death. No original Irish record currently cited on this profile identifies his birthplace or parents. A later descendant account by Ellen Glasgow says that Arthur came to America in 1766, aged sixteen and a ward, with his mother and elder brothers, and places the family's earlier Irish residence broadly in Counties Down and Antrim.<ref>Ellen Glasgow, ''The Woman Within'' (1954), appendix “A Dull Note for Genealogists,” pp. 298-299; excerpt reproduced at FamilySearch Memories, https://www.familysearch.org/en/memories/memory/16905684 (accessed 21 July 2026).</ref>

David Faris's 1990 genealogy of Robert Glasgow describes Robert as a son of James Glasgow of Moneymore and says that Robert migrated in 1769 with three brothers and a sister. The public catalogue summary does not name those siblings or expose the evidence supporting the Moneymore parentage.<ref>David Faris, ''The Glasgow Family of Adams County, Ohio'' (Baltimore: Gateway Press, 1990), WorldCat catalogue record 22731567, https://search.worldcat.org/title/22731567 (accessed 21 July 2026).</ref>

Arthur, Robert and Joseph are independently described as three brothers in the later history of Glasgow, Virginia.<ref>Town of Glasgow, Virginia, “History,” https://glasgowvirginia.org/history (accessed 21 July 2026).</ref> These accounts make a northern-Irish sibling cluster plausible but do not prove Arthur's attached parents or a specific Moneymore birth. One research hypothesis places an otherwise unrecorded older brother Adam, married to Maria, in Ireland as father of Adam Glasgow (born about 1758) and John Glasgow (born 1767). John's sons were Adam, James, John and Arthur, a sequence which could preserve his father, grandfather, himself and paternal uncle. The hypothesis is weakened because John's wife was Mary Arthur and therefore independently explains the name Arthur. No record presently names Adam in Arthur's family. Faris's James of Moneymore must not automatically be equated with the internally conflicted [[Glasgow-1024]] or the derivative [[Glasgow-3305]].

=== Probable Moneymore father — 17 October 2026 ===

'''Earlier research argument, superseded for fatherhood on 23 October 2026:'''
The existing Moneymore father account, Glasgow-1024, is assessed as the probable father of Robert Glasgow-12 and, by inference through their established brotherhood, Arthur Glasgow-649 and Joseph Glasgow-1543. The catalogue description of David Faris’s 1990 genealogy explicitly identifies the Adams County emigrant Robert (1749–1839) as a son of a James resident at Moneymore. It identifies a particular father and son, rather than offering a same-name local candidate. The family letter of 6 November 1806 printed by Faris names Arthur and Robert as Joseph’s brothers; Joseph’s 1831 will independently identifies Arthur as his deceased brother and the younger Robert as Arthur’s son. These sources distinguish the two Roberts and establish the sibling group to which the father attribution can reasonably extend. Robert’s pension supports the County Derry setting and 1769 migration. The approximate generations are compatible; the circa-1722 birth estimate is not independent evidence. The positive father attribution and established family group together warrant probable parentage, while remaining below documented or certain.

The father attribution survives here through a catalogue abstract of a retrospective genealogy; the book’s underlying parentage notes and a contemporary Irish parent record have not been inspected. The letter and will corroborate the sibling group, not the father’s name independently. Glasgow-1024 is used for its record-defined Moneymore father role: the inherited dates, Mary Harkness marriage, 1770 immigration, 1804 naturalisation, older James pedigree and proposed Corvanaghan identity are separate questions. The Corvanaghan identity and older father remain very uncertain. No probability is assigned to those claims by this review. The same father is inferred across the three established paternal-surname siblings; no evidence for different fathers has been identified. Other proposed siblings, including James-3305, John and Mary, and the proposed Adam connection are not upgraded.

Three existing father links change from an uncertain saved WikiTree flag and an ungraded/unknown local assessment to a formal probable local grade. No parent is newly attached, no live flag changes and no new working-tree component is created. All mothers remain separately uncertain; James’s own parents are unchanged. This is an inference from the combined existing evidence, not a newly discovered parent record.

=== Current research ===

[[Glasgow-649|Arthur Glasgow (Glasgow-649), born about 1750, later Rockbridge County, Virginia]] is now proved to be a brother of [[Glasgow-1543|Joseph Glasgow]] and [[Glasgow-12|Robert Glasgow]]. His claimed Moneymore birth and attached parents are still not established.

David Faris prints a family letter dated 6 November 1806 from Joseph and Betty Glasgow to Arthur. Joseph addresses Arthur as his brother and refers to “brother robert.” Joseph's 1831 will independently calls a younger Robert the son of his deceased brother Arthur and Joseph's nephew. The combined evidence makes the three-way sibling relationship strong; it does not identify their parents.

The repeated name <code>Arthur</code> in John Glasgow's descendants is real but heavily confounded by John's wife, '''Mary Arthur'''. Their son Arthur can naturally have been named from his mother's surname; later <code>Arthur Glasgow</code> compound names can honour that son or the maternal surname without referring to Arthur-649.

A useful working hypothesis remains: Arthur-649 could have had an older or half-brother Adam who remained in Ireland and became the older Adam implied by John-822's naming pattern. Faris calls emigrant Robert a son of '''James of Moneymore''', while later accounts make Robert, Joseph and Arthur brothers. The resulting <code>Adam-James-John-Arthur</code> sequence could preserve John's father Adam, grandfather James, John himself and his paternal uncle Arthur. No inspected source names Adam in that emigrant family, however.

This hypothesis concerns the record-defined '''James of Moneymore''', whose own dates and spouse are not supplied by the WorldCat summary. It must not be used to validate the internally conflicted live profile Glasgow-1024 or the wholly derivative James-3305.

This assessment draws on the cited records and public source material.<ref name="ProjectSource1">[https://www.virginiasar.org/assets/PROGRAMS/AMERICANHERITIAGE/RWGPreservation/2nd%20Edition%20VASSAR%20Rev%20War%20Burial%20Book%20Sep%2016%202022%20without%20illlustrations%20%282%29.pdf Virginia SAR Revolutionary War burial compilation].</ref><ref name="ProjectSource2">[https://glasgowvirginia.org/history Town of Glasgow history].</ref><ref name="ProjectSource3">[https://www.familysearch.org/en/memories/memory/16905684 FamilySearch Memories].</ref><ref name="ProjectSource4">[https://search.worldcat.org/title/22731567 WorldCat catalogue record].</ref><ref name="ProjectSource5">[https://swvirginians.wordpress.com/2014/12/12/joseph-glasgow-pulaski-co-va-will-of-1831/ Joseph Glasgow's 1831 will transcription].</ref>

=== Possible A. Glascow, 1794 arrival ===
A. Glascow from Glasgow is named with H. Jurriens from Riga and J. Mark from Königsbergen in a shipping-arrival report for 24 June 1794, under the Rotterdam dateline of 25 June.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/1335425007/ Rotterdamse courant, 26 June 1794, p.2].</ref>

Only the initial A. is given. The list probably names a shipmaster, but it does not state a vessel, full forename, sex, family or personal origin. Glasgow is the departure port. P. L. Markwaarden in the following entry is a different person.

This may concern [[Glasgow-649]]. Adult in 1794 and later migration is recorded in the known account account, but no maritime occupation or link to Rotterdam is known. Retained only as an age-compatible namesake lead.
